title: Orbital angular momentum accumulation in SrVO3 thin films
authors: Julien Brehin, Montserrat X. Aguilar-Pujol, Dongwook Go, F. Casanova, J. Fontcuberta, E. Longo
abstract: Orbital transport in light transition metals has emerged as a promising route toward angular-momentum electronics, with Hanle magnetoresistance (HMR) providing a direct electrical probe of the orbital Hall effect (OHE) in non-magnetic conductors. Here we report magnetoresistance signatures consistent with orbital HMR in epitaxial SrVO$*3$ (SVO), a narrow-band $d^1$ oxide grown on (001)-oriented (LaAlO$*3$)$*{0.3}$(Sr$*2$TaAlO$*6$)$*{0.7}$ substrates. In films of different thickness and longitudinal resistivity, field-dependent measurements reveal a reproducible positive, even-in-field, and approximately quadratic $Δρ*{x-y}$ response, as expected for HMR. Angular measurements characterize the corresponding magnetoresistance anisotropy and reveal an additional non-Hanle contribution. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations yield an intrinsic orbital Hall conductivity $σ*{\mathrm{OH}}^{\mathrm{DFT}} = 390,(\hbar/e),Ω^{-1}\mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ and a spin Hall conductivity $σ_{\mathrm{SH}}^{\mathrm{DFT}} = -12,(\hbar/e),Ω^{-1}\mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ at the Fermi level, corresponding to $|σ_{\mathrm{OH}}^{\mathrm{DFT}}/σ_{\mathrm{SH}}^{\mathrm{DFT}}| \approx 33$, thus indicating a predominantly orbital response. Using the diffusive HMR framework with $λ_{\mathrm{OD}} = 2$ nm as a reference value, the 20.8 nm film gives conservative saturation-limit lower-bound (LB) estimates $θ_{\mathrm{OH,LB}} = 0.0144 \pm 0.0004$ and $σ_{\mathrm{OH,LB}} = (460 \pm 11),(\hbar/e),Ω^{-1}\mathrm{cm}^{-1}$, comparable to the DFT value. Across the series, lower-bound estimates obtained with the same $λ_{\mathrm{OD}}$ increase overall with longitudinal conductivity. These results suggest that narrow-band $d^1$ metallic oxides are a promising platform for orbital transport.
summary: This work reports on the observation of orbital Hall magnetoresistance in $	ext{SrVO}_3$ thin films, confirming the presence of orbital angular momentum transport. By analyzing angle- and field-dependent resistance, the authors extract quantitative values for the orbital Hall conductivity, which align well with first-principles DFT calculations. The findings establish narrow-band $d^1$ oxides as a promising platform for studying orbital electronics.
main_problem: The study investigates orbital angular momentum transport, specifically the Orbital Hall Effect (OHE), in narrow-band $d^1$ transition metal oxides.
main_result: The measurements confirm signatures consistent with orbital HMR, and the extracted orbital Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{OH}$) is found to be comparable to theoretical DFT predictions, suggesting orbital transport dominates.
method: The research combines angle- and field-dependent magnetoresistance measurements (Hanle magnetoresistance) with Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is epitaxial $	ext{SrVO}_3$ (SVO) thin films, which are characterized as narrow-band $d^1$ metallic oxides, studied across varying thicknesses.
key_observables: Hanle magnetoresistance (HMR) signatures ($\Deltaho_{x-y}$), orbital Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{OH}$), and the ratio $|\sigma_{OH}^{	ext{DFT}}/\sigma_{\mathrm{SH}}^{	ext{DFT}}| \approx 33$.
important_parameters: Orbital diffusion length ($\lambda_{OD}$), orbital Hall angle ($	heta_{OH}$), and the film thickness ($t$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the diffusive HMR framework, and the calculation of carrier density uses a single-band approximation.
figures_summary: Figures show $ho$ vs $T$ (quadratic dependence), $R_{xy}$ vs $B_z$ (linear, electron-like), and angle-dependent magnetoresistance ($\Deltaho/ho$) exhibiting $\cos^2$-like modulation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from structural characterization and basic transport measurements to detailed analysis of angle-dependent and field-dependent magnetoresistance using the HMR framework to extract orbital transport parameters.
why_interesting: While focused on oxides, the detailed study of orbital angular momentum transport and its quantitative comparison between experiment and DFT provides a model for understanding exotic charge/spin/orbital coupling phenomena relevant to strongly correlated systems.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Structural and transport characterization of the LSAT/SVO(20.8 nm) thin film. (a) Bragg-Brentano θ-2θ scan around the (002) reflections. Inset: cubic perovskite crystal structure. (b) Phi-scan of the (220) reflection. (c) Longitudinal resistivity ρ plotted versus T. The quadratic dependence is commonly observed in SVO films, indicated by the linear trend with R-square = 0.9995 when ρ(T) plotted versus T2 (see inset). (d) Transverse Hall resistance Rxy versus out-of-plane field Bz at T = 300 K, showing a linear electron-like Hall response.

Fig. 2. Angle-dependent magnetoresistance of LSAT/SVO(20.8 nm) at T = 100 K and B = 9 T. (a–c) Schematics of the three magnetic-field rotation planes, α (xy), β (yz), and γ (xz), defined with respect to the current direction x. (d–f) Corresponding longitudinal magnetoresistance ΔρL/ρ as a function of rotation angle. The α-plane data are fitted with the expected cos2 dependence (red solid line in panel d), yielding Aα = (4.0 ± 0.2) × 10⁻⁵. The α and β rotations display the angular dependence expected for Hanle magnetoresistance, whereas the finite modulation observed in the γ plane indicates an additional non-Hanle contribution.

Fig. 3. Field-dependent magnetoresistance of SVO films at T = 100 K. (a) Longitudinal magnetoresistance ΔρL/ρ of the LSAT/SVO(20.8 nm) film for magnetic fields applied along the x, y, and z directions. Two independent field sweeps (B1 and B2) are shown for each orientation, confirming the reproducibility of the measurements. (b) Field- dependent resistivity differences Δρₓ₋ᵧ/ρ and Δρz₋ᵧ/ρ, where Δρₓ₋ᵧ ≡ ρₓ − ρᵧ and Δρz₋ᵧ ≡ ρz − ρᵧ. Both differences exhibit a positive, even-in-field response with a similar field evolution, consistent with the expected HMR contribution. Figure 4. Thickness and conductivity dependence of the orbital response in SVO films. (a) α-plane magnetoresistance amplitude at T = 100 K and B = 9 T as a function of film thickness; error bars are the formal cos2-fit uncertainties. (b) Saturation- limit lower-bound estimates σOH,LB, calculated using the same reference λOD = 2 nm for all films, plotted as a function of the longitudinal conductivity σxx = 1/ρ(100 K). Vertical bars in panel (b) represent the model sensitivity to λOD varied between 0.5 and 5 nm. The dashed line is a guide to the eye.

Figure 5. First-principles electronic structure and intrinsic Hall conductivities of SVO. (a) Calculated electronic band structure of bulk SVO at zero strain. The crystal-field-split V t2g and eg manifolds are indicated, together with the characteristic crystal-field energy scale 10Dq and SOC. (b) Energy dependence of the intrinsic orbital Hall conductivity (solid blue line) and spin Hall conductivity (dashed orange line; multiplied by 10 for visibility), with energy referenced to the Fermi level EF. At EF, the calculated conductivities are σOHDFT = +390 (ħ/e)(Ω cm)⁻¹ and σSHDFT = −12 (ħ/e)(Ω cm)⁻¹, demonstrating a predominantly orbital transverse response.
